year.shelter: Shoals in the warm shallows among the water plants, out of reach of bigger fish; deeper water in winter.
year.young: Hatched in spring from eggs laid in the shallows; a few centimetres long by their first autumn.

food.summer: Water fleas and small insect larvae.
food.winter: Eats very little under the ice.

year.notes: Young fish are the main food of perch from summer on, and of pike, grebes and terns. Shown at real size (about 7 cm): they are the young of world-scale fish, not part of the small world (ART.md).

text.title: Young roach
text.about_looks: A little silver fish, a few centimetres long, already with the roach's red eye.
text.about_food: Tiny water animals: water fleas and small larvae.
text.about_home: Shoals in the warm shallows among reeds and water plants.
text.about_winter: Moves to deeper water, where it stays a little warmer under the ice.
text.about_young: It hatched in spring from eggs stuck to water plants in the shallows.
text.about_fact: Perch, pike and many water birds eat young fish, so only a few grow up.
